book.title: The Penguin Book of Independent Crosswords, volume 1

clue.text: Displays personal decorations

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a military tattoo is a display of drumming and marching
second meaning: designs inked into the skin

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase about someone showing off their ornaments, but it splits into two meanings of the same plural word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is both an evening military pageant and an inked design on the body, so the plural covers both senses.

clue.text: Pay for freedom after the end of August, and beam

indicators.note: after says the payment comes after that letter
the end of a word is its last letter, here the last letter of August

parts.note: a ransom is a payment to free a captive

explanation.surface: A kidnap ransom is paid at the end of August, then someone beams with relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beam' looks like a smile but is the definition: a crossbar.
explanation.definitionFit: A transom is a horizontal crossbar in a window or above a door, a structural beam.

clue.text: Thrills about a thousand among rocky outcrops

indicators.note: among means placed in the midst of, so these letters go inside the outcrops

parts.note: tors are rocky hilltops, as on Dartmoor in England
re means about or concerning
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Climbers get excitement from some thousand crags.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor is a quiver, and a thrill is a shiver of excitement, so the two are close synonyms.

clue.text: A group of musicians etc. to get organised

indicators.note: getting organised means sorting into order, so the letters of the fodder are rearranged

explanation.surface: A band and their hangers-on need to sort themselves out.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is an ensemble of eight players or singers.

clue.text: In consequence the non-professional retired first — left

parts.note: so means therefore, in consequence

indicators.note: retired means gone back, so the lay word is read backwards

parts.note: laic means lay, not clergy or professional
1st, written IST, is first

explanation.surface: As a result the amateur stepped down first and walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a verb (departed) but is the political sense: on the left.
explanation.definitionFit: A socialist is on the political left, so left is used as a noun or adjective for that wing.

clue.text: Material for firing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: coarse cloth used for sacks
second meaning: dismissal from a job, being sacked

explanation.walkthrough: 'For firing' suggests fuel or a kiln, but firing here is dismissing an employee.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacking is a rough woven fabric, and sacking someone is dismissing them, the everyday slang sense of firing.

clue.text: Good man with bear

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good man
and means with, together with

explanation.surface: A kindly fellow is accompanied by a bear.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand something is to tolerate it, the same as being able to bear it.

clue.text: Cheat the stone-worker

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a swindler, from 'chisel' meaning to cheat
second meaning: one who carves stone with a chisel

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as an accusation against a mason, but it gives two separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Chisel is slang for defraud, so a chiseller is a con man; literally it is someone wielding a chisel.

clue.text: Cut off, and this is nothing new

parts.note: O is the round figure zero, nothing
late means recent, as in the latest news

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs that being disconnected is nothing new.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate something is to separate it, setting it apart from everything else.

clue.text: A little meagre, yes — that's most depressing

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone agrees a skimpy portion is the gloomiest thing of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey describes dull, cheerless weather or moods, so the superlative means the dreariest.

clue.text: Like the record? Twitch to it to get healthy

parts.note: like means as, as in 'as a rule'
an EP is an extended-play record
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a record is like and whether its jerky rhythm will do them good.
explanation.definitionFit: Aseptic means free from germs and infection, a sterile, sanitary sense of being healthy.

clue.text: Fat dunderhead in excellent position

indicators.note: in tells us the letter goes inside the excellent pair

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI
the head of 'dunder' is its first letter, D
a pose is a position held for a portrait

explanation.surface: An overweight fool has landed in a very comfortable post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dunderhead' looks like an insult but is split as the head of 'dunder', a lone D placed inside AI (A1).
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose is the technical adjective for animal tissue that stores fat, so it means fatty.

clue.text: Sign language

parts.note: not gestures for the deaf but a written system of symbols, a language of signs for fast note-taking

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase suggests signing with the hands; read literally, it is a writing system made of signs.
explanation.definitionFit: Shorthand, such as Pitman's, records speech using abbreviated symbols in place of letters, so it is literally a language of signs.

clue.text: Avoid notice in the evening

indicators.note: in tells us the notice sits inside the evening word

parts.note: eve is an old word for evening
an ad, or advertisement, is a public notice

explanation.surface: Someone tries to slip out unnoticed after dark.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to escape or dodge something, a plain synonym of avoid.

clue.text: Total over one hundred — sounds pleasing!

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the total word is read backwards

parts.note: a sum is a total
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A cash register or a score reports a total past a hundred, and the result is cheering.
explanation.definitionFit: Music is organised sound that delights the ear, so 'sounds pleasing' describes it as a noun phrase.

clue.text: Rival offer given preliminary study

indicators.note: given preliminary means the study comes first, before the offer

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn
a tender is a formal offer, as for a contract

explanation.surface: A competing bid is examined before the deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A contender is a competitor in a contest, someone vying against others.

clue.text: Reason for arranging in order make-up etc.

parts.note: to tell someone to do something is to order them

indicators.note: arranging signals a reordering of the abbreviation that ends the clue
make-up, as in rearranging the make-up of the letters, confirms they are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone justifies tidying their cosmetics and odds and ends into order.
explanation.walkthrough: IN is taken as written, TELL comes from 'order', and the letters of ETC are rearranged to ECT.
explanation.definitionFit: Reason in the sense of the mind's faculty for thinking is the intellect.

clue.text: Hardy girl keeping a quarter rent back for flat

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the other letters go inside the girl's name

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's heroine
S, south, is one of the compass quarters

indicators.note: back says the rent word is read backwards

parts.note: to let is to rent out

explanation.surface: Hardy's heroine holds a district where rent is owed on a flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like an apartment to go with the rent, but it means dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Food or wit that is flat has no flavour or zest, which is what tasteless means.

clue.text: Thinks to show spirit in a set-back

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a distilled drink

indicators.note: set-back read as set backwards, so the word set is reversed

explanation.surface: Someone shows their mettle when facing a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set-back' looks like one word meaning a misfortune, but the hyphen splits it into a word and its reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruminate is to ponder at length, chewing over a thought as a cow chews cud.

clue.text: Effecting miracle rescue

indicators.note: effecting means bringing about or making, so the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: A dramatic rescue pulled off by a miracle.
explanation.definitionFit: To reclaim something is to recover or win it back, saving it from loss.

clue.text: Consider one on the window-frame

parts.note: to mull something over is to consider it
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone thinks about the one standing on the window frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A mullion is the vertical bar dividing the lights of a window, part of its frame.

clue.text: Concerned with key changes for a stringed instrument

parts.note: re means concerning or about, as in a letter heading
B, E and C are each musical keys, so changing key three times gives three key letters

explanation.surface: A musician talks about modulating key on a stringed instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The rebec is a medieval bowed instrument, an early ancestor of the fiddle.

clue.text: A little bird — a member of the heron family

definitions.text: a member of the heron family

parts.note: a bit is a little
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A small bird turns out to be related to the herons.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a wading bird classed with the herons, known for its booming call.

clue.text: Bob is brusque and uppish certainly

parts.note: curt means brusque, short in manner

indicators.note: uppish means going upwards, so in this down entry the yes word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: yes means certainly

explanation.surface: Bob, a man's name, comes across as abrupt and certainly snooty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name; it is a quick bending of the knee.
explanation.definitionFit: To bob is to make a quick dip of the body, which is the curtsey a woman makes in greeting.

clue.text: Have offspring and get left in a hole!

indicators.note: in tells us the left letter goes inside the hole word

parts.note: a cave is a hole in rock

explanation.surface: A mother gives birth and ends up in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get left in a hole' sounds like being stranded, but it is a container instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A cow calves when she gives birth to a calf, so calve means to produce young.

clue.text: Actor's pet cavorting among the audience

definitions.note: describes a person who is one of the audience; the answer is the noun for such a person

indicators.note: cavorting means prancing about, so the letters frisk into a new order

explanation.surface: An actor's animal is capering about in the stalls.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator is a person who watches a show, one member of an audience.

clue.text: Passed a writer in the street

indicators.note: in tells us the writer goes inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: Someone walked by an author out on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that has passed is time spent, so passed and spent are synonyms.

clue.text: Get less light

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to narrow or diminish gradually
second meaning: a slender candle or wick for lighting

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as dimming a lamp, but the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A taper narrows towards a point and is also a thin candle used to light others.

clue.text: Conclude a revolutionary band will back a fabulous Greek girl

indicators.note: will back says the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: to end is to conclude
the IRA, the Irish Republican Army, is a revolutionary armed group

explanation.surface: A rebel group finishes and its people support a Greek girl of legend.
explanation.walkthrough: END, A and IRA together give ENDAIRA, and reading that backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Ariadne gave Theseus the thread to escape the labyrinth; fabulous here means belonging to fable.

clue.text: Taken from the newspapers, say

parts.note: ex means out of or from, as in 'ex works'
the press is the newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: A quotation lifted from the papers, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example', but it is the definition, the verb to say.
explanation.definitionFit: To express a thought is to put it into words, to say it.

clue.text: A body of serving men in quite new kind of tower

indicators.note: in tells us A and the engineers sit inside the new word

parts.note: mint, as in mint condition, means brand new
the RE, the Royal Engineers, is a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: A regiment of soldiers is housed in a newly built tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the slender tower of a mosque from which the call to prayer is made.

clue.text: An agent carrying jewellery has to be flexible

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so the jewellery goes inside the agent

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
a ring is a piece of jewellery

explanation.surface: A secret agent smuggling gems must be adaptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something springy bounces back when bent, so it is elastic and pliant.
